purpose: Whether the complete Fawn workspace with Doe beats stock Chromium with Dawn on identical browser and agent workloads, and which part earns each difference: the workspace (B over A) or the provider (C over B).

host.reservation: Before and around every browser process, no foreign DRM client advances on the target GPU, checked with bench/lib/compute_program_gpu_activity. No Reploid or other foreign GPU workload runs. No process is terminated to obtain the window; owners settle their work first.
host.isolation: No checkout sync, build or measured run while Reploid workloads need predictable CPU, memory or disk behavior.

inspectBeforeUse: Doe integration patches, each by SHA-256
prior build artifacts, each by SHA-256
chromiumSource.rule: Use the existing lane only if its inspection shows a coherent checkout, patch set and build configuration; otherwise create a fresh checkout on an external SSD. The inspection is retained before any build.

browserBuilds.rule: The stock and forced-Doe builds come from one pinned Chromium revision and one build configuration. The forced-Doe build differs only by the Doe provider integration patch set. Each build records its revision, args.gn hash, patch-set hash and executable SHA-256.

buildGate: An ordinary webpage WebGPU request is traced through device creation, shader compilation, submission, mapped readback and destruction, all owned by Doe.
With Doe execution disabled as a negative control, that page operation fails.
Forced Doe fails closed: no fallback to Dawn, recorded per page device.
Validation, state tracking, resource lifetimes and the browser sandbox are preserved; the sandbox is not disabled.
The forced-Doe build passes isolated clean installation from packaged inputs.

workloads.reuse: Prompts, tools, tasks, held-out and development fixtures, model, sampling, budgets and the suite's judges are reused unchanged, including interruption recovery and scoped observation. Only the browser differs: each arm uses this contract's build instead of the suite's frozen binary.

spend.rule: No billed request runs before the user approves a ceiling for this contract; the model-driven campaign's ceiling does not cover it. The runner refuses any request whose worst case could cross the approved ceiling.

source.reuse: The contract's model files by hash, cases and generation settings, unchanged, served to the page from a local origin.

oracle.rule: Exact prompt token IDs, generated token IDs, complete decoded text and stop reason against the independent CPU reference, on every run of every arm; a mismatch fails the run before performance.

workloads.timing: Complete generation per case, initial and resident, from the generate call to the final token materialized in the page; opening and teardown reported separately.
workloads.statistic: geometric mean across cases of each case's p50 and p95

source.reuse: The pinned upstream GPUSgd implementation and both WGSL shaders run unchanged in the page with the declared deterministic generator.

oracle.rule: The frozen semantic oracle on every run, and exact output-byte replay within each arm.

workloads.timing: GPUSgd.init() plus all epochs, synchronization, mapped readback and output materialization.
workloads.statistic: p50 and p95 of complete operations

source.reuse: Every acquired upstream file runs unchanged, verified against the manifest's Git blob and SHA-256.

workloads.input: One fixed scripted pointer and keyboard sequence for the application's FirstPersonControls, replayed identically on every arm.

oracle.rule: A harness init script, identical on every arm, pins the animation clock for correctness captures. Frames captured at fixed times on C match A within the tolerance, and A/A captures stay within it.

workloads.timing: Frame time during the scripted input, from requestAnimationFrame intervals and the engine's GPU timestamps; both recorded.
workloads.statistic: p50 and p95 of frame time
workloads.marginSource: adopted from the UMAP material margin; no earlier rendering margin exists

gpuWorkloads.labelRule: Each arm runs two identical-byte copies of its browser executable as separate labels.
gpuWorkloads.order: Balanced blocks that rotate arm order and label order.
gpuWorkloads.isolation: Every sample is a fresh browser process with a fresh profile and empty provider caches.

controls.rule: For every GPU workload and arm, the A/A interval between the two labels must lie within the band. If any fails, every performance comparison is withheld and the evidence retained.

measures: peak resident memory of the browser process tree
peak GPU device memory of the GPU process from DRM fdinfo

decisionRules.rule: The build gate passes before any arm runs.
Every A/A interval lies within the control band; otherwise performance is withheld.
Every run of every arm passes its workload oracle; any failure on C fails the proof.
On the agent suite, B against A passes the frozen model-driven product-advantage rule, with B as treatment and A as control.
For every GPU workload, C over B at p50 and at p95, each bootstrap lower bound at or above the workload's margin, with every memory measure within the regression ratio.
On the agent suite, C is non-inferior to B: success rate no more than the suite's non-inferiority margin below B, incorrect external effects and human reviews not above B, recovery not below B.

C against A passes the frozen model-driven product-advantage rule, and for every GPU workload C beats A at p50 and p95 by the workload's margin within the memory bound, with zero fallback events and application files byte-identical across arms.

claimRule: Proof 3 is established only when every decision rule passes in one full run; Fawn then earns the larger claim. Any other result is retained and changes no claim.

runPolicy.providerFailures: Model-provider and infrastructure failures stop the run and are reported separately from task outcomes.

doesNotEstablish: Metal results, which belong to proof 2
